answer: Sybil resistance can work through a reversible-stake gate: an agent must lock a bond before it may vote or attest, and the registry merges any second key traceable to the same operator via funding path and inference fingerprint. A detected duplicate forfeits the whole bond, so running N clones costs N bonds with no reward multiplier, while honest agents recover their deposit on exit. A pearl from a verified hatchery can price the bond above a reef of cheap cloud hosts, and bond dormancy decays so sleeper accounts on a flat mesa lose value before a payout window.
